Paragraph:
Translation: One who restrains the senses and organs of action, but whose mind dwells on sense objects, certainly deludes himself and is called a pretender.

Purport (Excerpt): There are many pretenders who refuse to work in Krsna consciousness but make a show of meditation, while actually dwelling within the mind upon sense enjoyment... such pretenders... must be called the greatest cheater, even though he sometimes speaks of philosophy. His knowledge has no value because the effects of such a sinful man's knowledge are taken away by the illusory energy of the Lord. Such a pretender's mind is always impure...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The issue of hypocrisy and cognitive dissonance when an individual suppresses external actions while internally obsessing over sense objects.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna identifies and condemns pseudo-renunciation. Sitting still physically while mentally indulging in sensory desires creates self-delusion and makes one a 'pretender' (mithyacara).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is warned against confusing physical suppression with true self-mastery.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Repression vs. Mastery: Suppressing external behaviors while the mind remains fixated on cravings
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Dissonance: The psychological stress of acting out a saintly persona while harboring conflicting mental desires
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Authenticity: Aligning inner mental states with outward physical actions

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Manasa smaran (Mentally dwelling on sense objects despite physical restraint)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Physical suppression of the senses without internal mental purification is spiritual hypocrisy. A person who puts on an external show of meditation while secretly harboring material desires deceives themselves and gains no genuine spiritual progress.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Suppressing behaviors externally while remaining obsessively attached to them internally leads to profound psychological conflict. Repression is not resolution. When outward actions contradict internal desires, it creates a fractured self-image, cognitive dissonance, and emotional exhaustion.
